text: When copying/adapting upstream pi example extensions into this repo, include README attribution with a link back to the original upstream example, following the existing notify README pattern.

For a future agent-workflow-audit extension, the user wants the distilled final audit results returned to the main session. The isolation goal is to keep intermediate discovery, command runs, raw errors, retries, and tool transcript out of the main session context, not to hide the final report.

The gnosis pi extension is intentionally agent-facing only: it exposes a gnosis tool but does not add user slash commands because the user explicitly said commands were unnecessary. Keep future UX changes aligned with that unless requested.

The unified Fast extension should be added without deleting or replacing the existing openai-fast and claude-fast standalone packages. The root @diegopetrucci/pi-extensions bundle should auto-load only the unified extension; the two provider-specific Fast extensions remain available as standalone packages but become standalone-only.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: npm 11.17.0 can produce byte-different gzip wrappers for the same package when run under Node 24.11.1 versus Node 26.5.0, even though the gunzipped tar payload bytes are identical. This surfaced while manually bootstrapping @diegopetrucci/pi-fast@0.1.0 before the Node 24-pinned OIDC workflow. Release verification must compare exact tar payloads as a bounded fallback rather than assuming gzip-level hash reproducibility across Node runtimes.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: The standalone openai-fast and claude-fast extensions are retired. Future Fast mode work should target only the unified extensions/fast implementation; do not extend the retired standalone variants.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Decision history for project-mcp-json: initially a Claude-style per-file approval (path+sha256) was built because Pi auto-trusts dirs with no Pi-recognized protected resources, so a root-only .mcp.json would otherwise run with no prompt. User then rejected the separate approval: 'if the dir is approved already the mcps should be too', and wants alignment with Pi's own trust semantics (incl. parent-dir trust inheritance). Current design: treat root .mcp.json like a Pi trust-requiring resource — require isProjectTrusted; accept Pi's real decision when protected resources exist; else nearest-ancestor saved trust.json decision; else defaultProjectTrust (ask => skip + suggest /trust). The extension never writes trust.json. Out of scope: Codex .codex/config.toml import, parent-dir .mcp.json discovery.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: The published @diegopetrucci/pi-claude-fast and @diegopetrucci/pi-openai-fast packages stay in the repo so those npm names keep resolving, but their extension bodies are deprecation notices that do not read config, register commands, or mutate provider requests. The collection continues to load only extensions/fast. This supersedes keeping them as working standalone Fast implementations.
author: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>
